ideas.title: The ice breaks
ideas.critique: This is the next step of the glass sea, and a real one: floes that tilt under weight and tip friends into the sea would be buoyancy and contact the island has never had. The risk is the last two ice and stomp takes, which were drifting friends and blinking ground. If the tilt and slide don't read on film, this becomes another 'the sea changed' post.

ideas.title: Letters that are real paper
ideas.nearest: Me, to cut out and fold
ideas.critique: A sheet that flutters, side-slips, slides off a roof and folds in the wind is cloth and aero physics the island has never shown. It is tied to the human's own act of writing a wish, so they see their own note fall. Lumi catching it at the end is the scripted part, and the shell sim has to look like paper rather than a falling tile, or it is just a prop drop.

ideas.title: Lumi's printer
ideas.nearest: Me, to cut out and fold
ideas.critique: This carries out the printer the human's goal names almost word for word, so it is capped and predictable. A part growing layer by layer is mostly an animation. Only the moment the printed part tips over when set down badly is simulated.

ideas.title: A clockwork walker
ideas.critique: A toy that walks because its gears mesh by contact and its spring runs down is an engineered mechanism. Nothing on the island has moved by its own workings like that, and a waddle that ends face-down is clip-worthy. It depends on the gait truly emerging from the sim. A scripted walk with spinning gears on top would collapse it to a prop with a parade.

ideas.title: The wobble tower
ideas.critique: This is a well-known party-game recipe, so the premise surprises no one. But the human pulling a block against real friction while a 30-block stack holds or collapses is the most playable physics pitched here, and friends taking turns by character gives it a second life. It is strong on fun and realism, weak on novelty.

ideas.title: Lumi gets a soft body
ideas.critique: FEM squash and jiggle in place of keyframes is a deep step for both animation and Lumi's self, and it lasts: every later film inherits it. It is the third Lumi-body piece in a short span, though, and a subtle jiggle easily reads as nothing in a film. The dent from a hug has to be unmistakable.

ideas.title: The pond splashes
ideas.critique: Real FLIP water reacting to bodies is overdue and squarely in the goal's water example, which caps its surprise. The crown, rings off the bank and a bobbing leaf would still be the first liquid the island has. The splash contest gives it a reason to watch again, but it is the obvious use of water.

ideas.title: Snowballs that break
ideas.critique: Bonded clusters that burst into lasting crumbs are a real fracture effect, and the player can join in, which helps. A snowball fight is the most predictable winter scene there is, though. The hat knocked off is a scripted gag tacked on.

ideas.title: Real skaters
ideas.critique: This swaps a disc model for rigid bodies on the same ice. A friend tipping onto its back and spinning legs-up would be funny, but the step is mostly invisible unless that tip-over happens. It reads as a backend refinement of a post that already looked like drifting.

ideas.title: The bending tree
ideas.critique: A wind-flexed trunk and apples rolling down to the path are solid but expected nature physics, and the chase down the hill echoes the rolling-ball posts. The rod sim is real, but the payoff is gentle and easy to predict.
